newsitem.title: TURKEY: Cement maker Turk Baticim sales up in H1.
newsitem.headline: Cement maker Turk Baticim sales up in H1.

text.p: Turkey's cement and ready mixed concrete producer Bati Anadolu Cimento A.S. (Baticim) increased its total sales by 6.02 percent to 806,325 tonnes in the first half of the year, a senior company official said on Tuesday.

"We sold 6.02 percent more cement in the first half and increased our turnover to 8.48 trillion lira ($51.8 million in the first half of 1997) from 4.00 trillion in the first half of 1996," Esref Baltali, board member of the company, told Reuters.
"We exceeded our five percent real growth target in the first half with a 15 percent real growth, which made it easier to meet the annual targets," he said.
The company reported 2.77 trillion lira net profit in the first six months of the year, up from 877 billion lira in the same 1996 period.
Shares of the company opened at 17,000 lira on Tuesday on the Istanbul Stock Exchange and closed unchanged.
Baltali estimated a five-percent growth for the Turkish cement sector, compared to a 15-percent growth for Baticim in 1997. He expects another five-percent growth in the sector next year.
"Our target is to increase our market share in the region to 55 to 60 percent from its 45 percent level," he added.
Baticim aims to increase its turnover to 18 trillion lira in 1997 from 9.5 trillion lira in 1996, and increase the pre-tax profit to eight trillion lira from 3.12 trillion lira.
In the first six months of the year the company's clinker production rose by 6.79 percent to 719,233 tonnes and cement production by 7.55 percent to 805,285 tonnes.
Necip Terzibasioglu, general manager of the company, said domestic sales of Baticim increased by 13.56 percent to 707,475 tonnes but exports sank by 28,13 percent to 98,850 tonnes in H1.
Baticim targets to produce and sell 1.55 million tonnes of cement in 1997.

Baticim plans to break ground in late August to build a clinker mill and cement packaging facility in Burdur in south-west Anatolia, near the country's main touristic area where the tourism-based construction sector is booming.
The 300,000-tonne capacity plant will be completed by the end of 1998 with spending $10 million.

Baltali said Baticim's Izmir plant did not need any capacity expanding investments in view of the current market conditions but money would be spent on some environmental and modernisation projects. ($ = 163800 Turkish Lire)
